description_full: IBEX Limited provides end-to-end technology-enabled customer lifecycle experience solutions in the United States and internationally. The company's products and services portfolio includes ibex Connect that offers customer service, technical support, revenue generation, and other value-added outsourced back-office services through the CX model, which integrates voice, email, chat, SMS, social media, and other communication applications; ibex Digital, a customer acquisition solution that comprises digital marketing, e-commerce technology, and platform solutions; and Wave iX, an AI customer experience platform. It operates customer engagement and customer acquisition delivery centers. The company serves government, banking and financial services, delivery and logistics, health tech and wellness, high tech, retail and e-commerce, streaming and entertainment, travel and hospitality, and utility industries. IBEX Limited was formerly known as IBEX Holdings Limited and changed its name to IBEX Limited in September 2019. The company was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in Washington, District Of Columbia.

Each employee generates $800 of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $198 per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 105× revenue per employee (high relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: IBEX Limited is a small-cap technology business with a $760M market cap on $644M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 33% against a 9% cost of capital — a 24-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $31M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.27× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 59× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 1.9%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 4.1% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

Cybersecurity liability and talent cost inflation — a single breach can erase years of goodwill, and the war for engineering talent compresses margins even at scale.

sect: Its 9% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 26% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 2% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 40% and a beta of 0.84, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.23 vs 5y 0.72), so read it loosely.

The 2 covering analysts target $46.50 on average, 18% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 4.1% annual cash-flow growth, 11pp less than the model expects.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.2% over 3 years.

Analysts expect 7.2% long-term annual earnings growth.
